title: At the clothing store
goal: Buy clothes, give sizes and colors, and point things out with ce, cet, cette, ces.
bekal: pointing things out with *ce, cet, cette, ces*
colors and sizes that agree in gender
trying on, comparing, and saying no politely

dialogs.title: Dialogue — Je peux essayer ?
dialogs.intro: Budi is looking for a jacket for the fall. A sales assistant comes over.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Oui, je cherche une veste pour l'automne.
lines.id: Yes, I'm looking for a jacket for the fall.
lines.literal: yes, I search a jacket for the-autumn.

lines.speaker: Vendeuse:
lines.text: Cette veste bleue est très populaire. Quelle taille ?
lines.id: This blue jacket is very popular. What size are you?
lines.literal: this jacket blue is very popular. which size?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Je fais du quarante, je crois.
lines.literal: I make some forty, I believe.

lines.speaker: Vendeuse:
lines.text: Voilà. Vous pouvez essayer, la cabine est là-bas.
lines.id: Here you go. You can try it on — the fitting room is over there.
lines.literal: there-it-is. you can try, the cabin is over-there.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Merci… Elle est un peu grande, non ?
lines.id: Thanks… It's a bit big, isn't it?
lines.literal: thanks… it is a-little big, no?

lines.speaker: Vendeuse:
lines.text: Un peu. Vous voulez essayer ce modèle en trente-huit ?
lines.id: A little. Would you like to try this style in a thirty-eight?
lines.literal: a-little. you want try this model in thirty-eight?

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Volontiers. Vous l'avez en noir aussi ?
lines.id: Sure. Do you have it in black too?
lines.literal: gladly. you it-have in black also?

lines.speaker: Vendeuse:
lines.text: Oui, en noir et en gris. Le noir est plus élégant.
lines.id: Yes, in black and in gray. The black is more elegant.
lines.literal: yes, in black and in gray. the black is more elegant.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Elle coûte combien, cette veste noire ?
lines.id: How much is it, this black jacket?
lines.literal: it costs how-much, this jacket black?

lines.speaker: Vendeuse:
lines.text: Quatre-vingt-neuf euros. Il y a une réduction cette semaine.
lines.id: Eighty-nine euros. There's a discount this week.
lines.literal: four-twenties-nine euros. there-is a reduction this week.

lines.speaker: Budi:
lines.text: Parfait, je la prends. Vous acceptez la carte ?
lines.id: Perfect, I'll take it. Do you take cards?
lines.literal: perfect, I it take. you accept the card?

notes: **Je fais du quarante** is how the French give their clothing size. Literally "I make some forty". For shoes: *je fais du quarante-deux* or *je chausse du quarante-deux*.

**Colors agree with the noun.** *Une veste **bleue**, un pantalon **bleu**, des chaussures **bleues**.* ⚠️ Some colors never change because they were originally nouns: *marron* (chestnut), *orange* (the fruit), and compound colors like *bleu clair*, *vert foncé*.

**Je la prends** — *la* here stands for *la veste*. Object pronouns like this are A2 material and you don't have to master them yet, but you'll hear them constantly in shops, so learn to spot the pattern: the pronoun goes **before** the verb, not after it as in English ("I take it").
**Volontiers** (voh-lohn-TYAY) = gladly, sure. A polite, very French yes. Its cousins: *avec plaisir*, *je veux bien*.
**Essayer** needs an object or none at all: *je peux essayer ?* is enough at the fitting room. Its forms bend a little because of the y: *j'essaie, tu essaies, nous essayons*.
**Une réduction** = a discount. Other words you'll see in shop windows: *les soldes* (the official sales, twice a year), *une promo*, *moins 30 %*.
**Vous pouvez essayer** — a polite offer. Note that the second verb is always in the infinitive after *pouvoir*, *vouloir*, *devoir*. This gets unpacked fully in the next unit.

grammars.title: Ce, cet, cette, ces — pointing things out
body: One word that replaces *le/la/les* when you point to a specific thing in front of you. English has "this" and "that"; French uses one form for both.
after: *Cet* and *cette* sound **exactly the same**: seht. The difference is only in writing — a spelling trap that catches many learners in exams.

If you need to separate "this" from "that", add **-ci** and **-là** to the end of the noun: *cette veste-**ci*** (this jacket) versus *cette veste-**là*** (that jacket). Use it only when you really need the contrast.

grammars.title: Colors
body: Ordinary adjectives, so they follow the rules of Unit 11. The interesting part is the exceptions.
after: ⚠️ *Marron* and *orange* never change: *des chaussures marron*, *une veste orange*. That's because both are names of fruits borrowed as colors.
Compound colors freeze too: *une veste bleu clair*, *des yeux vert foncé*. As soon as there's a second word, the whole combination stops changing.

blocks.title: Phrases for the store
items: *Je cherche un pull.* — I'm looking for a sweater.
*Je peux essayer ?* — Can I try it on?
*Quelle taille faites-vous ?* — What size are you?
*C'est trop grand / trop petit / trop serré.* — It's too big / too small / too tight.
*Vous l'avez en bleu ?* — Do you have it in blue?
*Ça vous va très bien.* — It really suits you.
*Je vais réfléchir.* — I'll think about it. (a gentle no)

blocks.text: *Je vais réfléchir* is the most useful way to say no in all of French. Polite, painless, and every seller understands it as "not buying" without anyone having to say so.
